recommendations: Open with a warm introduction, explain your role and the purpose of today’s visit, outline confidentiality and its limits, and invite the patient to co-create an agenda (e.g., ‘We’ll focus on your anxiety today, then review options’).

Use empathy and open-ended prompts before closed screens: reflect (“It sounds frustrating and exhausting”), then ask broad questions about anxiety (“Can you walk me through a recent day when worry felt overwhelming?”).

Conduct a structured DSM-5 GAD assessment (excessive worry most days ≥6 months, difficulty controlling worry, 3+ symptoms: restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance, impairment) and briefly rule out differentials (MDD, panic, PTSD, OCD, substance/caffeine, medical contributors).
